## I dispatched a bug that was already fixed -- read the comments, not the status field

Sent an agent to implement bff5 as live and untouched. It was neither: change 2551 merged two days
ago, the Terraform was applied under operator approval, and the ticket's own FIVE comments record the
entire arc. The agent correctly declined to duplicate landed work and wrote no code.

MY ERROR, precisely: I dispatched off the board's STATUS FIELD (in_progress) plus my task-list entry,
without reading the ticket. Every brief I write tells agents to 'read every comment' and 'verify the
specifics against the tree rather than re-deriving'. I did not apply either to myself before writing
one. Status said in_progress because the last AC is an operator action, not because the code was
outstanding -- a status field cannot distinguish 'not started' from 'done but for one human step',
and the comments could.

Cost: one agent run. Recovered value: an INDEPENDENT verification against origin/main that I would
otherwise have taken on trust from earlier in this session -- the landed commit b987b87f15a1, all 15
rebar/host alarms breaching bar the one marked exception, the mirror_out_of_sync else-branch fix
publishing oos=1 rather than 0 (publishing 0 would have preserved the fail-open), and the guard
selecting on namespace with an anti-vacuity floor rather than a hand-list. It also re-proved the
guard's teeth by mutation. That is worth having, but it is not what I asked for and I should not
pretend the dispatch was clever.

WHAT REMAINS ON bff5: only AC3's production step -- inducing a real Gerrit-REST/ls-remote failure and
confirming mirror_out_of_sync reaches ALARM rather than merely emitting a datapoint. That is
deliberate production fault-injection and an operator decision. So bff5 is NOT closeable by me
autonomously, and I have marked it accordingly rather than leaving it looking like open engineering
work.

HABIT ADDED: before dispatching any ticket, read its comments and check for a merged change carrying
its rebar-ticket trailer. 'in_progress' means someone touched it, not that work is outstanding.

Also worth noting the same trap nearly applied to 3276 and 9ea3, which I was holding for FILE
CONFLICT reasons. Both may likewise be further along than their status suggests. I will read their
comments before dispatching rather than assuming.
